title: How much of Earth is near the equator?
hook: 30° is a third of the way to the pole. Is 30°S to 30°N a third of the Earth?

knows: what the equator and poles are
doesNotKnow: that equal steps of latitude do not cover equal areas
that half the Earth's surface lies within 30° of the equator

misconception: Equal steps of latitude cover equal areas, so the band within 30° of the equator is about a third of the planet.
objective: The learner can explain that area grows with the sine of latitude, so the band from 30°S to 30°N, a third of the degrees, holds half the surface, while the cap beyond 60°N holds under 7%.
keyState: The 30°S–30°N band shaded with both readouts (33.3% of the degrees, 50% of the surface), and the 60°N-to-pole cap compared (6.7%).

claims.text: Half of the Earth's surface lies between 30°S and 30°N.
claims.source: Area of a spherical zone 2πRh (Archimedes' hat-box theorem; any geometry text, from memory) gives the share (sin n − sin s)/2 = (0.5 + 0.5)/2 = 0.5. Demo.tsx surfaceShare; the drawn band polygon's geoArea gives 0.5000 (builder node run). On the real ellipsoid the figure differs by under 0.2% (cm-geography brief). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Node: (sin30 - sin(-30))/2 = 0.5.

claims.text: The band from 30°S to 30°N is a third of the latitude range (60° of 180°).
claims.source: Arithmetic: 60/180 = 33.3%. Demo.tsx rangeShare. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Re-derived; no issue.

claims.text: The cap from 60°N to the pole spans 30° of latitude but holds only about 6.7% of the surface.
claims.source: (sin 90° − sin 60°)/2 = (1 − 0.866)/2 = 0.0670; geoArea of the drawn cap 0.0670 (builder node run). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Node: (1 - sin 60)/2 = 0.0670.

claims.text: Area grows with the sine of latitude, not with the degrees: sin 30° is one half, so half of each hemisphere lies within 30° of the equator.
claims.source: From c1: the area from the equator to latitude φ is 2πR² sin φ, half of a hemisphere (2πR²) at φ = 30°. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Re-derived; no issue.

claims.text: Other bands on the stage: 10°S–10°N holds 17.4% of the surface and 60°S–60°N holds 86.6%.
claims.source: sin 10° = 0.1736, sin 60° = 0.8660 (builder node run). Readout values only. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 6): Node: sin 10 = 0.1736; sin 60 = 0.8660.

recall.question: Which holds more of Earth's surface: the band from the equator to 30°N, or everything from 30°N to the North Pole?
options: From 30°N to the pole, because it spans twice the degrees
recall.why: Area from the equator grows with sin(latitude); sin 30° = 1/2, so each holds exactly a quarter of the globe, though one spans 30° and the other 60°.
